display_name: National Insurance Law ss 334 and 337 and Schedule J, with the s 1 definitions they use: the reduced collection threshold, the rates of insurance contributions per branch and per column of insured person, and the arithmetic that applies them

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). Hebrew is quoted only in `-- src:N |` comments generated mechanically from line N of the deposited source by tools/srcquote.py, and in short runs that tools/hebcheck.py checks occur verbatim in it. Schedule J's figures are generated from the source by tools/schedule_j.py.

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval

published_figures.note: Figures the Law computes but does not print, taken from the National Insurance Institute's pages fetched 2026-10-06; URLs and sha256 in nii-il04-published-figures.l4 and NOTES.md section 7.

scope: Encoded: s 334(a) (its three definitions, the reduced collection threshold and both update paragraphs) and (b); s 337(a)(1), (a)(2) (for monthly advance periods), (b) (as the test whether an order is within the power) and (c); Schedule J in full, both tables, all items, figure columns and totals, with the editors' 2024-2027 notes; s 1 'employee', 'employer', 'self-employed person', 'the average wage' (with 'compensation', 'the compensation rate', 'update day'), 'the index', 'tax year', 'the Minister'. Every other s 1 term is listed out of scope. Inputs, not encoded: s 335 (which branches a person pays), ss 344-351 with s 348 and Schedule K (the income), s 342 (the deduction, row IL-05), s 336, s 340, s 2, s 28, s 32, Schedule A. Declined by name where they reach a case: s 341 (reduced rates by order), s 343 (reduced work-injury contributions), work injury of one who is neither (s 340(a)(2)), a '–' in the person's column, the temporary column D gap, contribution months before 2026, and the threshold for 2027 on unless supplied. See NOTES.md sections 1-3.

years_answered.contribution months: January 2026 on; earlier months declined (the deposited s 334 and Schedule J are in force from 1 January 2026)
years_answered.reduced collection threshold: 2026 from the Institute's published figure; 2027 on only when the caller supplies it (index-updated 2027-2028, wage-updated from 2029)
years_answered.Schedule J version: 2026 temporary table with the 2024-2027 item-4 figure; 2027 permanent table with the 2024-2027 item-4 figures; 2028 on permanent table as printed

expected_red.why: Schedule J's printed totals differ from the sums of its items in 10 cells across the four readings of the schedule; and the Institute's 2026 composite rates above the threshold (employee 14.6, deduction 7, controlling shareholder 14.17 and 6.79) exceed the sums of the items in 4 cases. Findings about the source, not defects of the encoding: NOTES.md section 0, fork F4.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source. No independent test pass was run (the row was briefed as one session with no sub-agents); every expected value in the tests modules was worked out before it was asserted, by a computation over the source's cells and the Institute's printed figures that does not use this encoding.

check.note: The 14 errors are exactly the 14 expected failures of nii-il04-tests-expected-red.l4; nii-il04-tests.l4 is 120 of 120 satisfied. check.sh exit 0.

forks.F1: Schedule J's years are the calendar years of the months for which contributions are paid.
forks.F2: Each table's 2024-2027 notes apply while that table is in force (the readings coincide in effect).
forks.F3: The temporary version's column D headings leave the part of a wage between the threshold and 60% of the average wage without a figure; declined (the Institute applies the upper figure from the threshold).
forks.F4: Ten printed totals differ from the sums of the items; the items are used for computing, the totals are data, compared red.
forks.F5: Which average wage (s 1, 13,566, or s 2, 13,769 for 2026) the slice means is not decided; every rule takes it as an argument.
forks.F6: A fall in the index or the average wage lowers the threshold (the formula as written).
forks.F7: Nothing is rounded; the 2026 threshold is used as published.
forks.F8: s 337(a)(2): equal shares over the advance periods; monthly periods only, others declined.
forks.F9: s 337(c): the deduction is multiplied by the ratio of the new rate to the old.
forks.F10: A '–' is no figure, not a zero: a branch paid with a dash in the person's column is declined.
forks.F11: Whether the relative of a family-member employee is an 'employer' is not decided (no rule here turns on it).
forks.F12: A tax year is a calendar year; special assessment periods are not modelled.
forks.F13: The core of 'employee' is a person employed within an employment relationship (an input).
forks.F14: s 334(b)'s 'the payer is the employer' is recorded as a comment only.
forks.F15: Schedule J items 1 and 2 are one maternity branch; the column decides which item applies.
forks.F16: 'at least' and 'not less than' in 'self-employed person' are inclusive.
forks.F17: Column C is marginal: each figure on its part of the income.
